title: Release gate: query error budget status during deploy + override token support
author: Sahana Iyer
description: Summary: Introduces a deploy-time release gate step that queries the control plane for current error budget status (scoped by tier + service) and posts a structured outcome back into CI. Includes an override token mechanism (TTL + reason) for emergencies, with audit logging and redaction to avoid leaking credentials. Context: As part of Tiered SLOs + Error Budget enforcement (ENG-2422), we need a consistent way for teams to “feel” budget burn in the deploy workflow. This PR wires the existing budget-check endpoint (added in #18421) into our CI/release tooling and standardizes the contract for warn-only vs block behavior. What’s in this PR: (1) New CI step `budget_gate` used by deploy pipelines to call `POST /internal/reliability/error-budgets/check` with `{tier, service, region(optional), rollout_id(optional)}` and a request timeout of 2s. (2) CI annotations + build summary: posts one-line status (“OK”, “AT_RISK”, “EXHAUSTED”, “UNKNOWN”) plus links to the relevant SLO dashboard + policy doc. (3) Fail/allow policy: supports `mode=warn` (default) and `mode=block` (behind feature flag `release_gates.error_budget.blocking`) so we can roll out gradually. If the endpoint is unavailable, we mark as UNKNOWN and allow in warn mode, but still emit a metric + event for follow-up. (4) Override tokens: gate can be bypassed with `BUDGET_OVERRIDE_TOKEN` (scoped token minted by oncall tooling, TTL enforced by control plane). The CI step requires an `OVERRIDE_REASON` string; the reason + token hash are recorded to audit logs. Tokens are redacted from all logs/annotations. (5) Policy checks: ensures overrides are only accepted for allow-listed services while we’re in pilot (initial allow-list: gateway, routing, control-plane). (6) Documentation: adds a short runbook section for interpreting gate output and how to request an override via oncall. Testing: unit tests for gate decision logic + redaction; contract tests against a local stub; staging deploy (hosted tier, warn-only) with manual budget states. Rollout plan: enable step in warn-only for pilot services first; once burn-rate alerting and budget computation are stable, switch to soft-block/hard-block via config (separate change). Notes: This PR intentionally does not change any commercial SLA language; it’s internal enforcement plumbing only.
commits: ci/release: add budget gate step wrapper + config parsing
control-plane client: implement error budget check call + retries/timeouts
policy: add allow-list + mode gating flag for blocking behavior
security: redact override token from logs/annotations; add structured audit fields
docs: add release gate usage + override procedure
tests: unit + contract tests for gate outputs (OK/AT_RISK/EXHAUSTED/UNKNOWN)
ci_checks: Buildkite: redwood-main (deploy pipeline) ✅ | Unit tests ✅ | Lint ✅ | Security scan ✅ | Contract tests (stubbed CP) ✅. Initial run failed on lint due to shellcheck warnings in budget_gate.sh; fixed in 6b2e4a1 and reran successfully.
conversation: Benji Okafor (review): Can we guarantee we don’t log the override token anywhere? The shell step currently echoes the full command on failure. Also please confirm we don’t include token in CI annotations. Sahana Iyer (author): Good catch. Updated step to disable xtrace for token-bearing commands, added explicit redaction helper, and added unit test asserting token never appears in emitted JSON/annotations. Ethan Park (review): What’s the failure mode if control plane is slow/down? We should avoid blocking deploys due to the budget service itself, at least in warn-only. Also suggest a hard 2s timeout with a single retry. Sahana Iyer (author): Implemented 2s timeout + 1 retry (jittered). If still failing, gate returns UNKNOWN and allows in warn mode; in block mode we fail closed (explicitly documented). Added metrics `release_gate_budget_check_unknown_total` to track this. Aisha Bello (review): Please make sure the status mapping matches the policy doc: AT_RISK should be triggered on multi-window burn rate thresholds, not just “< X% remaining”. Also can we include a link to the runbook for exhaustion response in the CI message? Sahana Iyer (author): The gate only consumes the control plane’s computed status (OK/AT_RISK/EXHAUSTED) and does not recompute locally; clarified in docs. Added runbook link to the annotation payload. Connor O'Brien (review): Override needs accountability: require reason and capture who/what invoked it. Also can we ensure this is restricted to pilot services for now? Sahana Iyer (author): Added required `OVERRIDE_REASON` (CI step errors if token present but reason missing). Control plane logs include actor (CI service account), repo/pr/build URL, reason, token hash, TTL. Added allow-list enforcement + config flag to expand later. Jordan Lee (review): Minor: please align the request payload keys with what policy engine expects (`tier` values: hosted|dedicated, `service` matches service registry). Sahana Iyer (author): Updated to use canonical tier enum + service registry name; added validation with a clear error message when a pipeline misconfigures the service name.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Ethan Park on 2026-02-10. Follow-up tracked in ENG-2427 to enable warn-only on additional services and validate false positives before moving to soft-block.
release_notes: Internal: CI deploy pipelines now surface error budget status during releases (warn-only by default) and support audited override tokens for emergencies.
